title: Heat Pump Rebates in Edmonton 2026: CEIP at 6% and the Rules
desc: Edmonton heat pump help for 2026: no City or provincial rebate, CEIP financing from $3,000 to $50,000 at a fixed 6.00%, a three-upgrade rule, and why air conditioners don't qualify.
lead: Edmonton has no cash rebate for a heat pump in 2026. The City says so on its own page: there are no City residential rebates available right now. What Edmonton offers is the Clean Energy Improvement Program, which finances upgrades at a fixed 6.00%. It has a few rules that matter a lot for heat pumps, so here they are in plain words.
cards_heading: What an Edmonton home can use for a heat pump
cards_intro: We re-read the City of Edmonton's CEIP page and Natural Resources Canada's program page on October 3, 2026. Sources are at the bottom.

cards.title: Edmonton Clean Energy Improvement Program
cards.note: Financing at a fixed 6.00%, repaid on your property tax bill for up to 20 years. The program is nearing capacity, so new pre-qualifications are queued and handled first come, first served.

cards.title: City of Edmonton rebates
cards.note: The City's CEIP FAQ says there are currently no City residential rebates.

cards.title: Oil to Heat Pump Affordability (federal)
cards.note: July 31, 2026 was the last day for Alberta residents to apply.

cards.title: Canada Greener Homes Grant
cards.note: The grant has ended, and the Greener Homes Loan approves no new applications.

after_cards:
Edmonton's three-upgrade rule

Edmonton's CEIP finances a home only when at least three upgrades are installed. A heat pump on its own is usually not enough. A typical bundle might be a heat pump, a heat pump water heater and attic insulation. The exceptions: fewer upgrades are allowed if they get the home to net zero, or if you have used CEIP on that property before.
sections: What Edmonton will and won't finance

Edmonton is stricter than most Alberta cities. Its CEIP page lists three things that are not eligible in Edmonton:

  • Air conditioners. The City suggests a heat pump instead, since it cools as well as heats.
  • High-efficiency gas furnaces, unless combined with a heat pump.
  • High-efficiency storage water heaters. A heat pump water heater or a tankless gas heater is allowed.

So if your furnace is old and you also want summer cooling, the path CEIP supports is a heat pump paired with a furnace for backup, plus at least one more upgrade.

The 2021 Census counted 396,395 households in Edmonton. Half live in single-detached houses, and 64% own their home. About 41% of households live in homes built before 1981, a higher share than Calgary's 35%. That includes 70,205 owner households in detached houses built before 1981.

Those mid-century houses are where a three-upgrade CEIP bundle fits best. They often need insulation and a new heating system at the same time, which makes the three-upgrade rule easier to meet.
Heat pumps in an Edmonton winter

Edmonton's average January low over the last ten years was about -14.3°C, and the coldest reading was -41.2°C. That is cold for any heating system. A cold-climate heat pump can carry a home through much of the winter, but you should plan backup heat for the deepest cold. Ask each installer the lowest outdoor temperature the unit is rated to run at, and how your home will stay warm below it.
How CEIP payments work in Edmonton

Repayment goes on your property tax bill, and the term is the shorter of 20 years or the useful life of the upgrades. If you are on the monthly tax payment plan, the CEIP charge is split into monthly payments too. You can pay off any upgrade early, with no penalty.

Timing matters. Upgrades finished between May and December 15 show up on the next May tax notice with no interest yet. If you pay that first charge in full by December 15, you avoid interest. After that, interest starts and appears on the following year's notice.

The City's first $20 million is meant to fund about 300 home projects, and intake pauses after 150 pre-qualifications. That is why new applications are queued.

faq: Is there a heat pump rebate in Edmonton?

Not in 2026. The City of Edmonton says it has no residential rebates right now, Alberta has no provincial heat pump rebate, and the federal Oil to Heat Pump program closed for Alberta on July 31, 2026.
What is the Edmonton CEIP interest rate?
The current tranche is a fixed 6.00%, for up to 20 years or the useful life of your upgrades, whichever is shorter.
Can I finance just a heat pump through Edmonton CEIP?
Usually not. Edmonton requires at least three upgrades, unless fewer get the home to net zero or the property used CEIP before.
Will Edmonton CEIP pay for a new gas furnace?
Only if it is combined with a heat pump. A high-efficiency gas furnace on its own is not eligible in Edmonton.
Can I combine CEIP with other rebates?
Yes. The City encourages you to use any municipal, provincial, federal or utility incentive alongside CEIP.
